problem: Section pages need a small label above each heading to number and name sections (a kicker). No artifact provides one, so consumers improvise it: six instances on the designauthority concept page alone, each re-inventing size, tracking and colour.
insufficiency: resolve('a section kicker label above a heading') -> UNDEFINED (top candidates component/acc, component/badge, component/page-head all scored 4.00 vs 6.50 needed; no recipe matched). Closest artifacts misfit: component/acc is an accordion control; component/badge is an interactive status chip with dot semantics; component/page-head is the page-level header block, not a section eyebrow. search_authority for eyebrow / section label -> no artifact.
reuse_case: Long-form documentation and concept pages across consumers: the designauthority site numbers six sections with it; Triage spec and review pages need the same eyebrow element for their section structure. Any page that numbers its sections repeats this need.
composition_check: Badge composes status, not structure (interactive, dot-prefixed). page-head owns the page title block and cannot express '01 - The promise' above an h2. Raw mono text at --fs-pre-log leaves case, tracking, colour and spacing unbound, and consumers diverged in exactly those four properties during the concept page's own audit. A small typographic element is required; no existing artifact composes to it.

proposed.name: kicker
proposed.sketch:
Section eyebrow label:

, uppercase applied via text-transform over sentence-case source, --fs-pre-log size, letter-spacing token, --text-secondary colour, small margin below before the heading it precedes; optional numeric prefix. Token-only, static text, no border or background.

tests.description: kick renders uppercase via text-transform (source text stays sentence case) and uses only tokens, no raw px/hex
text colour resolves to a text token with at least 4.5:1 contrast on the page surface
static text only: no interactive states, border or background
